title: The impact of Generative AI chatbots on behavioral intention in travel planning: A theory of consumption value perspective
content:
by Ying Wei, Jialin Zhang

Generative AI (GenAI) chatbots are revolutionizing online travel planning by transitioning travelers’ focus from merely gathering information to obtaining personalized recommendations and facilitating seamless bookings. Grounded in the Interactive Technology Acceptance Model and Consumption Value Theory, this study investigates how the attributes of GenAI chatbots, specifically personalization and anthropomorphism, alongside user traits such as self-efficacy and personal innovativeness, influence travel planning intention through perceived value. Data collected from a questionnaire survey were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). The findings reveal that GenAI chatbot attributes (personalization and anthropomorphism) and user traits (self-efficacy and personal innovativeness) exert significant direct positive effects on perceived values. The indirect effects of anthropomorphism, personalization, self-efficacy, and personal innovativeness on adoption intentions are most pronounced through hedonic value, followed by utilitarian value, with novelty value playing the least prominent mediating role. This study enriches the theoretical understanding of AI-based customer service and provides tourism businesses with insights into enhancing GenAI’s features and shaping consumer perceptions.
